headline: Frequent Flyer Retains 12-Year-Old Daughter To Hand-Stamp Boarding Passes To Maintain Emotional Stability
body:
For software consultant Rohan Mehra, the government’s decision to end the manual stamping of international boarding passes has triggered a deep psychological void, prompting him to hire his 12-year-old daughter, Aanya, to perform the task manually before every flight. Mehra, who holds a collection of over 400 stamped passes dating back to 2012, insists that the physical sensation of the stamp hitting the paper is the only thing that confirms he is actually departing the country.

"The digital boarding pass just feels like a suggestion," Mehra explained while watching Aanya apply a red ink pad to his phone screen at the IGI departure lounge. "Without the sound of the 'thwack' and the slightly smeared ink, I feel like I might just be walking into a high-end mall instead of boarding a Boeing 787. Aanya has really stepped up; she even practiced her 'indecipherable official signature' for three weeks to ensure the authenticity of the experience."

Aanya, who currently charges her father one extra hour of screen time per stamp, admits the role is demanding but rewarding. "Dad gets very anxious if the ink isn't smudged properly or if the date stamp doesn't have a slight tilt to the left," she noted while preparing her kit. "He says the stamp is his security blanket, so I make sure to do it with the same level of bureaucratic indifference he’s come to love."

Airport authorities, while acknowledging the new policy, have confirmed that as long as Mehra is not using an actual government seal, they see no issue with his personal ritual. Mehra remains undeterred by the inconvenience, already planning to train his daughter to conduct a 'random' bag inspection before he reaches the gate to keep his travel experience feeling traditional.
caption: When the government moves to modernize, some of us just aren't ready to let go of the sweet, sweet sound of a rubber stamp. How are you coping with the loss of travel stationery? #TravelMemories #AirportLife #StampingOutTradition (satire)

sourceHeadline.title: India to end boarding pass stamping at airports for international travellers from September 1

The father-daughter dynamic adds a layer of 'affectionate ribbing' and genuine warmth that the other entries lack, as the others mostly descend into cynical portrayals of 'identity crises' or litigiousness.
